payload.notes: Start at (0,0). Vertical corridor; up leads to a junction, down appears a dead end. Move up.
At junction (0,1). Explore the long left corridor first; track position by successful moves and use wall-following/DFS.
At (-1,1), continuing left along the corridor to inspect its endpoint before backtracking.
Continuing left toward the corridor endpoint; backtrack right once blocked or at the terminal junction.
Continue left along the corridor toward its endpoint; record the terminal structure before backtracking.
At (-4,1), continue left to inspect the remaining corridor endpoint before backtracking.
Continue left toward the corridor endpoint; inspect the terminal cell, then backtrack right if no branch or exit appears.
Reached the corridor endpoint; after confirming no branch or exit, backtrack right toward the junction.
Dead-end confirmed at (-6,1). Backtrack right along the corridor to the junction, then investigate branches.
Backtracking right from the dead end toward the junction; continue along the corridor and inspect the next branch when reached.
At (-4,1), continue right to the known junction at (0,1), then investigate its downward branch.
Returning right toward the junction; continue along the corridor, then investigate the downward branch at (0,1).
Continue right toward the junction at (0,1); investigate the downward branch once there.
Returned to the junction after exploring the left dead end. Investigate the downward branch next.
At (0,1), exploring the downward branch; track any new junction or exit.
At (0,-1), inspect the downward dead end; if blocked next, backtrack up and investigate the unvisited right branch at (0,1).
Backtracking up from the lower dead-end; continue up to the junction, then explore the unvisited right branch.
At the lower vertical corridor after backtracking one step. Move up toward the junction, then explore the right branch.
At (0,-1); move up to the central junction, then explore the right branch.
At the central junction; left and down branches are explored dead ends. Explore the unvisited right branch.
At (1,1), the right branch is a dead-end upward/right. Follow the open downward corridor to inspect its endpoint and junctions.
At (1,0), continue down through the vertical corridor to inspect the endpoint and any junction.
At (1,-1), continue down to inspect the remaining corridor and any exit or branch.
At (1,-2), the downward corridor has reached a junction with an unexplored left branch. Move left to investigate it.
At (0,-2), the left branch is blocked. The downward route is unexplored; proceed down and track any junction or exit.
Continue down the unexplored corridor; record any junction or exit.
At (0,-3), the downward corridor appears to end, while the right branch is unexplored. Move right to investigate it.
Right was blocked at (0,-3). Continue down along the open corridor to inspect its endpoint; backtrack if it is a dead end.
At (0,-4), continue down along the open corridor to inspect its endpoint; backtrack upward if it is a dead end.
At the apparent dead end. Backtrack upward toward the junction visible three cells away; investigate its right branch when reached.
Backtracking upward from the lower dead end toward the junction three cells ahead; continue up before exploring its unvisited right branch.
Continue upward toward the unexplored junction and its right branch.
At (0,-3), the newly revealed right branch is open and unexplored. Move right to investigate it.
At the newly explored right branch. Continue down along the open corridor toward its endpoint and inspect for an exit or branch.
At (1,-3), continue down the unexplored corridor toward the lower junction; inspect for an exit or branch.
At (1,-5), vertical corridor continues both ways. Explore downward toward the lower junction; backtrack if it dead-ends.
At (1,-5), continue down toward the revealed lower junction and inspect its left branch.
At the lower corridor endpoint/junction after moving down. The left branch is open and unexplored; investigate it.
At (0,-6), continue left along the unexplored corridor to inspect its endpoint and any branches.
Continue left along the unexplored corridor; inspect the next cell for a branch or exit.
Continue left through the unexplored corridor, checking the next junction for an exit or branch.
At (-3,-6), both up and right are unexplored. Choose up first; inspect the upper corridor and backtrack if it dead-ends.
At (-3,-5), upward cell has an unexplored left branch. Move up to inspect it, then backtrack if needed.
At (-3,-5), continue upward to inspect the branch revealed ahead; track any exit or junction, then backtrack if necessary.
Up is blocked, so remain at (-3,-5). Explore the open left branch; backtrack if it ends without an exit.
Exploring the left branch from (-3,-5); continue left toward its endpoint, then backtrack if no exit or new branch appears.
Continue left along the unexplored branch toward its endpoint; inspect for an exit or junction, then backtrack right if it ends.
At the newly reached junction, right backtracks along the explored corridor while down is unexplored. Choose down to continue DFS exploration.
At (-5,-6), continue down into the newly revealed junction to explore its branches.
At (-5,-6), the downward route is unexplored and leads to a junction. Continue down to investigate its branches and search for the exit.
At (-5,-7); down is blocked. Explore the unvisited left branch, then inspect its upward opening.
At (-6,-6) after moving left. The unexplored upward branch is open; follow it and inspect for the exit or new junction.
At (-6,-5), continue upward toward the visible junction at (-6,-2) and inspect its branches for the exit.
Continue upward to the junction; inspect its right branch for the exit.
At the junction after moving up. The downward route is explored; take the unexplored right branch and continue searching for the exit.
At (-5,-3) after entering the right branch. Left backtracks; explore the open upward route for the exit.
At (-5,-2), up and left are blocked. Explore the open right branch; backtrack down if it ends without revealing the exit.
At (-4,-2), right and down are blocked. Explore the open upward branch; record any exit or junction, backtracking left if it dead-ends.
At (-4,0) after moving up. This junction has three open branches; continue upward first to explore for the exit, backtracking if it dead-ends.
At (-4,1), upward move reached a corridor with open left and down. Explore left first; backtrack right if it becomes a dead end.
At (-5,1), continue left toward the known corridor endpoint; after confirming the dead end, backtrack right and explore remaining branches.
At the left corridor endpoint. Backtrack right toward the junction, then explore the remaining down branch.
Backtracking right from the left endpoint toward the junction; continue right and inspect the remaining downward branch.
At (-4,1), the left route is explored. Take the open downward branch and continue DFS exploration toward any exit.
At (-4,-1), continue down the unexplored branch; inspect for an exit or new junction.
At the three-way junction after moving down. The upward route is explored; investigate the open right branch first, then return to explore down if needed.
Right is blocked. Both open routes are known, so backtrack upward to the junction and continue systematic exploration of any remaining branch.
At a three-way junction after moving up. Explore the open right branch, recording any new junction or exit.
At (-3,-1), right is blocked and left backtracks. Explore the open downward branch for an exit or new junction.
At (-3,-2), continue down the unexplored corridor toward the junction ahead; inspect for an exit or new branch.
At (-3,-2), continue down toward the visible junction and inspect its branches for the exit.
Exit is visible one cell to the left. Move left immediately.
